The present appeal preferred by the insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeks to assail the award dated 12.10.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claim Tribunal in MACT Petition No.1037/08/05.

He,
however, does not assail the quantum of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: However, while learned counsel for the appellant contends that in the light of this admitted position that the respondent no.1 was a gratuitous passenger, it was a clear case of breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and therefore the appellant cannot be directed to pay compensation, learned counsel for the respondent contends otherwise, her plea being that in the facts of the present case, the learned Tribunal was justified in directing the appellant to pay the awarded amount and then recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
5. In order to appreciate the rival submissions of the parties, it would be apposite to refer to the relevant findings of the learned Tribunal on this aspect.

The same read as under:-
"It is thus evident that the claimant being a person who had boarded in the goods carrying vehicle in said circumstances was a gratuitous passenger in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy and was not covered under the insurance policy.

sentences.text: The facts of that case in nutshell was that deaths of some persons and injury also had taken place in a motor vehicular accident due to negligent driving of motor vehicle described as Tata 407 which was admittedly insured against third party risk with the insurer.
The claim on account of injuries was passed under Section 166 of M.V. Act.

The insurer of the offending vehicle resisted the said claims denying its liability, raising the defence that it could not be made accountable to indemnify as there was breach of terms and condition of the insurance policy, there being no valid permit taken out in respect of the offending vehicle and the victims being gratuitous passengers.

The Tribunal held that there was a breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, however, declined to exonerate the insurer and instead called it upon to satisfy the awards granting it recovery rights against the owner of the offending vehicle.
The above said appeals were pressed by the insurer/appellant only to contend that instead of being called upon to recover it should have been fully exonerated.
The Hon'ble Delhi High Court did not find fault with the approach of the Tribunal.

It held that the third party interest has to be taken care of and that the Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Nafe Singh & Ors on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32602017/

The Hon'ble Delhi High Court did not find it a case to make any interference and dismissed the appeals.
The said judgment is squarely applicable on the facts and circumstances of the present case.

In view of the above settled law, the insurance co/R3 is not being exonerated but instead it is directed to satisfy the award amount, however, it is granted recovery rights against the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. R2 namely Surender Singh.

6. In the light of the aforesaid, while I am inclined to agree with learned counsel for the appellant that the insurer cannot be held liable to pay compensation for injuries caused to a gratuitous passenger, the fact remains that in such cases, the Court can, in appropriate cases, direct the insurer to pay compensation and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

The learned Tribunal has after noticing the decision of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs.
Manju Kanwar & Ors (supra) has followed this very course of action.

7. At this stage, reference may also be made to the decision Manuara Khatun and Ors. v. Rajesh Kr.
Singh and Ors., AIR 2017 SC 1204, wherein the Apex Court despite finding that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as a gratuitous passenger and was therefore, not covered under the insurance policy, had by applying the principle of 'pay and recover' directed the insurer to pay compensation to the claimant and thereafter recover the same from owner of the offending vehicle.

9.
The appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.

10.Since the appellant has already deposited the awarded amount with the Registrar General of this Court, the Registry is directed to forthwith release the same alongwith accrued interest thereon in favour of the claimants.

11.As the appeal is being dismissed, learned counsel for the parties jointly submit that the statutory amount of Rs.25,000/- be paid to any deserving widow who has lost her husband during the pandemic of Covid-19.
